decision_log.decision: Organise the room on its long east-west axis: table on the axis, all built-ins consolidated into one low horizontal band along the north long wall, the service aisle along the glazed south wall, kitchen at the west end and living room at the east end.
decision_log.rationale: The dining room is treated as one bay of a long living-dining bar: it flows from the kitchen door past the table to a leafless passage beside the core, and every element is a long horizontal band many times wider than high under the low 2.40 m ceiling.

decision_log.decision: Kitchen door 0.90 x 2.20 m on the west short wall at its south corner (offset 0.10 m), inward-opening, hinged on the south jamb; plain flush oak leaf, no architrave, surround or step.
decision_log.rationale: Doors are kept few, flush and plain; the leaf swings back toward the solid south-west return so its swing zone (x 0.00-0.90, y 0.10-1.00) sits in the aisle and never strikes a glazed leaf or any furniture.

decision_log.decision: Second connection as a leafless 1.22 x 2.20 m opening at the south end of the east wall, the remainder of that wall read as the blank coursed-brick face of the chimney core beyond.
decision_log.rationale: The dining room opens past the core to the living room in a straight line from the kitchen door, with no expressed doorway, so the two rooms read as one space.

decision_log.decision: South wall as a ribbon of three outward-swinging glazed door leaves 0.84 x 2.20 m between 0.38 m brick piers on a 1.22 m module, with a continuous head at 2.20 m, offset to the east end and leaving a 0.76 m solid return at the kitchen corner.
decision_log.rationale: The south wall of the dining room is almost entirely glazed doors onto a balcony, gathered into one ribbon of tall narrow lights under a continuous head; the band is stopped short of the west corner so the kitchen door can open back against brick, which also makes the wall asymmetrical rather than a centred composition.

decision_log.decision: Straight-line leaded lattice in every glazed leaf: tall narrow border lights, a field of shallow lozenges about three times as wide as high, small square lights in the top tier.
decision_log.rationale: Where glazing is detailed it carries a straight-line geometric leaded pattern; the lozenge proportion follows the measured pattern. Used in all three leaves, accepting that the evidence is mixed.

decision_log.decision: Built-in banquette along the north wall (x 1.20-4.80) made as a low brick wall: coursed brick plinth to 0.38 m, plain cast-stone seat slab, leather cushion to 0.49 m, stippled wool back pad and an oak stepped top rail at 0.90-0.96 m; three dining seats at the table, the eastern 1.20 m running on to the core wall as a side seat.
decision_log.rationale: Low brick walls with plain light copings are the base element; the seat is a coping slab on a plinth, with every profile built from stacked rectangular layers and no carving, turning or mantel-like ornament.

decision_log.decision: Built-in sideboard at the kitchen end of the north wall (x 0.00-1.20): the same brick plinth, two flush oak doors, a cast-stone top slab at 0.90-0.96 m aligned with the bench rail, and a cantilevered cast-stone shelf slab 1.20 x 0.25 x 0.06 m with its top at 1.52 m.
decision_log.rationale: The service piece is offset to one end so the built-in wall reads as an asymmetrical stepped composition - a taller short block at the kitchen end and a long low bar - rather than a centred symmetrical one; the shelf is a plain slab markedly wider than high.

decision_log.decision: No fireplace or hearth in the room.
decision_log.rationale: The hearth belongs in the central masonry core on the long axis between living and dining rooms, never on an outside wall; in a single rectangular room every wall is a perimeter wall, so the core is implied beyond the east wall and no hearth is built here.

decision_log.decision: Materials: tawny facing brick on all walls with raked bed joints and flush colour-matched perpends; plain honed cast-stone caps, slabs and a 0.90-0.96 m string course; hardwax-oiled oak for all joinery; leather and stippled wool; stippled lime-plaster frieze panels in oak frames at 1.90-2.20 m; tawny-red quarry tile floor in running bond with courses east-west. No mirrored panels; no gloss lacquer on any wall.
decision_log.rationale: Brick reads as horizontal courses only, every edge is capped by a plain light band, textured infill panels sit in a framed band at the top tier, and the floor's coursing continues the horizontal banding.

decision_log.decision: Palette: tawny brick and red tile as dominants, light cast stone as the neutral strip between them, oak, saddle leather, umber wool and brushed copper as warm accents; warm putty lime plaster for frieze and ceiling.
decision_log.rationale: Dark warm brick bands between plain light horizontal strips, with warm accents of tile, copper and oak.

decision_log.decision: Proportions: table 2.40 x 0.90 x 0.74 m (2.67:1, low); chairs 0.42 m wide x 1.25 m high (about 3:1, tall narrow backs); glazed leaves 0.84 x 2.20 m (2.6:1) on a 1.22 m module split 0.84 leaf / 0.38 pier; bench 3.60 m long with a 0.49 m seat; flat 2.40 m ceiling with no beams or drops.
decision_log.rationale: Long low horizontals for the furniture and ceiling, tall narrow lights in the band, and the measured pier-to-pier module with its leaf-and-pier subdivision.

decision_log.decision: Lighting: continuous concealed dimmable LED in the coved soffit of the oak head band on all four walls; three stepped oak box pendants with leaded glass panels and copper liners over the table (underside 1.60 m); concealed strip under the sideboard shelf slab.
decision_log.rationale: The stepped head band with a coved soffit becomes the light source, keeping the low ceiling plain; the pendants are built up from stacked rectangular layers and straight-line leaded glass rather than turned or ornamented fittings.

decision_log.decision: Seating count: 3 on the banquette, 3 chairs on the south side, 1 chair at each end = 8 dining seats.
decision_log.rationale: Meets the brief's eight seats with the fixed seating on the wall side and loose chairs on the aisle side so the aisle stays clear.

decision_log.decision: Circulation: one straight aisle 1.65 m clear (y 0.00-1.65) from the kitchen door to the east passage; 0.70 m strips beyond the end chairs; glazed leaves swing out; nothing in the kitchen-door swing.
decision_log.rationale: Exceeds the 0.90 m clear path required; the sideboard is served from the strip west of the table; the 0.70 m end strips are for sitting, not through passage.

decision_log.decision: Flush floor throughout: no level changes or raised thresholds at any opening.
decision_log.rationale: Doors sit flush at floor level with no step, path or surround; inside, nothing is stepped.

conflicts.constraint: Brief defines a single rectangular 4.80 x 3.60 m dining room; no fireplace is asked for and no central masonry core can sit inside the room, so any hearth here would be on a perimeter wall.
conflicts.resolution: Brief favoured: no hearth is built. The rule is applied only by implication - the east wall is treated as the blank brick face of the core beyond and the leafless passage runs past it - and R03 is cited for the axial organisation and the passage, not for a built hearth.

conflicts.constraint: Brief requires a 0.80-1.00 m kitchen door on a short wall with nothing in its swing; an inward-opening door at the south-west corner would strike a glazed leaf if the ribbon ran the entire south wall.
conflicts.resolution: Brief favoured on buildability: the ribbon is three leaves (x 1.14-4.42), stopping 0.76 m short of the west corner so the kitchen door can lie back against solid brick; the rule is kept for the remaining 3.68 m of the wall and for the leaf, pier and head pattern.

conflicts.constraint: Brief requires a labelled kitchen door and at least one further opening, while the rule prefers as few doors as possible and no expressed entrance.
conflicts.resolution: Brief favoured: both connections are provided. The rule governs their treatment - a plain flush oak leaf in a plain frame for the kitchen door, a leafless opening to the living room, no architrave, surround, step or threshold change at either.
